subject: CloudScale pilot — capacity contingency & budgeting
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: CloudScale pilot — capacity contingency & budgeting

Hi team,

CloudScale just pushed the pilot kickoff to the top of their priority list and asked if we can guarantee capacity for their 6-week pilot starting May 6. HubSpot deal HS-44821 shows a likely initial QPS that maps to ~4 concurrent H100s for the first two weeks, then scaling down to 2 H100s + burst A100 capacity for inference.

Questions I need answered for the weekly fleet planning call tomorrow:
- Can infra guarantee 4x H100 sustained for 2 weeks starting 2028-05-06? If not, what's the contingency?
- What's the cost delta (hosted/dedicated) for committing reserved capacity vs. using burst credits?
- Finance: what confirmation do we need from CloudScale (PO/term sheet) before we convert an internal reservation to a commit?

I've attached the pipeline snapshot and a lightweight allocation matrix (below) for reference. I'd like to land an interim plan during tomorrow's triage so sales can give CloudScale a clear answer by EOD Friday.

Attachments: pipeline_snapshot_20280422.xlsx, capacity_allocation_matrix.csv

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudScale pilot — capacity contingency & budgeting

Thanks Marissa — quick read of the snapshot: CloudScale lands in our high-confidence bucket (deal stage: pilot-commit, ARR upside ~$1.2M). From a sales perspective I recommend we commit to the conservative plan below so we don't lose momentum:

- Reserve 4x H100s (sustained) for 2028-05-06 to 2028-05-20 (two-week heavy phase)
- After week 2, scale to 2x H100 + 8x A100 burst slots for 4 weeks

If finance needs more confidence before converting to a paid reserve, we can offer a hybrid: commit to reserved capacity for week 1 (discounted) and rely on burst credits for week 2 pending PO. That gives CloudScale the guarantee they want while reducing our exposure.

Next steps: Ben, can you outline the minimum procurement milestone you need to clear the fully-reserved option? Karthik, does infra have a short-term capacity window we can draw from without hurting other committed customers?

-Laura

On Apr 22, 2028, at 08:15, Marissa Cole wrote:

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudScale pilot — capacity contingency & budgeting

TL;DR: we can probably swing the two-week H100 window but not without moving some burst pools and bumping a couple of non-critical dev pools to queued runs. Contingency plan below.

Capacity notes:
- H100 inventory currently: 24 total; 12 reserved across existing Dedicated deals; 6 in active use; 6 free/burst pool.
- To guarantee 4x sustained for two weeks we need to:
  1) migrate 2 dev jobs to queued scheduling (estimated 36–48hr delay)
  2) borrow 2 H100s from burst pool (reduces burst headroom for other customers)

Contingency options if finance can't sign off on full commit:
A) Hybrid commit: reserve 2 H100s + 4 A100 burst slots; provide CloudScale with a rollback timeline for additional H100s if PO clears by week 2.
B) Canary approach: start pilot on reduced instance (2 H100s + high-QPS batching) and validate SLOs; if metrics hit targets by day 3, spin up remaining H100s (automated playbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-allocation-contingency).

Operational impacts:
- We will need to surface this to the fleet scheduling Slack channel and tag owners for the dev work migration.
- Also recommending we earmark 20% of burst credits for CloudScale to avoid noisy neighbor problems while we transition.

Happy to discuss in the triage call.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure

On Apr 22, 2028, at 09:03, Laura Bennett wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudScale pilot — capacity contingency & budgeting

Finance take (short): we can greenlight a short-term internal reservation for week 1 (operational approval) with a refundable hold if CloudScale provides a signed PO and standard payment terms by 2028-05-03. The math: moving 4x H100 from burst to reserved for two weeks is ~ $75k net revenue-at-risk vs. $120k in expected pilot consumption; hybrid pricing protects us.

Required artifacts to finalize a fully-reserved commitment:
- Signed PO or Net-30 procurement agreement (procurement@cloudscale.com)
- Confirmation of anticipated throughput + model size (ops@cloudscale.com) — we have the snapshot, but need verifiable usage estimates

I'll attach the payment terms we usually use for pilots and a short estimation worksheet. If sales can get verbal PO + procurement alignment by EOD Friday I can sign off on the week-1 internal hold and start the internal billing hold process.

Attachments: cloudscale_payment_terms.pdf

-Ben
Head of Revenue Finance

Thanks everyone — summary and action items below (for the triage call Monday):

Summary decision draft:
- Week 1 (2028-05-06 to 2028-05-12): place internal hold for 2x H100s (ops hold), convert to full 4x H100 reserved if signed PO arrives by 2028-05-03. Ben will prepare billing hold and refund terms.
- Week 2 (2028-05-13 to 2028-05-20): keep burst-backed 2x H100s + 8x A100 burst slots; auto-escalate to reserved if PO clears by day 3 of week 2.
- Canary fallback: start pilot with 2x H100s, validate latency/throughput day 1–3; infra to auto-scale remaining capacity via playbook if metrics meet thresholds.

Action items:
- Laura: push for signed PO / procurement alignment (target EOD Fri, 2028-04-27).
- Ben: draft billing hold + refund language; finalize cloudscale_payment_terms.pdf (Ben, due Tue EOD).
- Karthik: prep runbook changes and tag owners for dev-job migrations; confirm whether the 20% burst earmark is configurable (due Mon morning).

Attachments included: pipeline_snapshot_20280422.xlsx, capacity_allocation_matrix.csv.

If no objections I'll present this as the tentative plan in tomorrow's fleet planning meeting and ask for formal sign-off by Finance/Infra by Tuesday.

— Marissa
